series_key: developing a robot in python and mql5
idea_name: GMM-clustered features into XGBoost binary path classifier
mechanism: Features are clustered with sklearn GaussianMixture (GMM), then RFECV selects ~20 features into labeled_data_engineered. An XGBClassifier(objective='binary:logistic') is trained on rows before FORWARD to predict labels where a favorable path exists: price moves beyond take-profit (~200 pips) without the stop (~100 pips) being touched. Live sense is the classifier probability / hard class for long(1)/short(0).
data_needed: Engineered numeric features per bar; GMM cluster assignments; binary labels from prior-article labeling; FORWARD date cut; optional GridSearchCV over max_depth/learning_rate/n_estimators
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Price series with pip-based TP/SL labeling; train≈2000–2010, test≈2010–2019, exam from 2019; custom tester exits at i+48 bars; historical span cited 1990–2024
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a concrete neural/sequence-adjacent sensor: GMM soft regimes on engineered features feeding a boosted classifier of asymmetric R:R path outcomes rather than raw next-bar direction.
quote: here we are talking about forecasting situations when the price has changed by more than the take profit (200 pips) and has not touched the stop (100 pips) with its tail

series_key: developing a robot in python and mql5
mechanism: test_model simulates every predicted label: long on 1 / short on 0, entry at close[i], exit at close[i+48], subtract markup (spread/commission proxy) from P&L in point_cost units, accumulate balance and plot equity with a FORWARD vertical marker. Converts classification accuracy into USD path quality under costs.
data_needed: Model predictions on X_test; close prices aligned to index; markup; initial_balance; point_cost; FORWARD timestamp
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same labeled price frame; 48-bar holding horizon; markup example 0.00001
why_new_for_mis: A cost-aware horizon-P&L sensor MIS can attach to any classifier—flags when label accuracy is real but markup-adjusted equity still drains (or vice versa).
quote: Trading is simulated using the model predictions: long at 1, short at 0. If the profit exceeds the markup, the position is closed and the profit is added to the balance.

series_key: developing a robot in python and mql5
mechanism: Data are cut into train (≤FORWARD), test (≥FORWARD, ≤EXAMWARD usage varies), and exam (>EXAMWARD never seen in train/tune). Author trains 2000–2010, tests 2010–2019, exams from 2019; accuracy falling 73%→60% while remaining profitable is treated as evidence the concept (low-risk/high-reward path) survived a regime cut.
data_needed: Datetime-indexed feature/label frame; FORWARD and EXAMWARD cut dates; accuracy and custom-tester equity on each segment
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi-decade price history; exam mimics unknown future from 2019 onward
why_new_for_mis: Explicit three-zone temporal regime-change probe MIS can reuse: score sensors by how little path-classification quality collapses across successive out-of-time cuts.
quote: I conducted training on data from 2000-2010, test on 2010-2019, exam - from 2019. The exam simulates trading in an unknown future.

series_key: developing a robot in python and mql5
idea_name: Bagged XGBoost ensemble on risk-reward path labels
mechanism: Multiple XGBClassifiers are trained on different subsamples (bagging) with per-model GridSearchCV; predictions are combined. Reported classification accuracy of trades with risk-reward 1:8 rises to ~73% versus earlier single-model ~53–56%, with the ensemble framed as learning low-risk/high-profit situations.
data_needed: Bootstrap/subsample partitions of train features/labels; per-model hyperparameter grids; aggregation rule for ensemble votes/probabilities
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same binary path-label task with 1:8 R:R framing; forward/exam charts shown after ensembling
why_new_for_mis: Ensemble disagreement / vote margin on asymmetric R:R path labels is a usable confidence sensor for MIS when admitting trade-path opportunities.
quote: The accuracy of classifying trades with a risk-reward ratio of 1:8 increased to 73%.

idea_name: Point-normalized MA geometry shapes as perceptron inputs
mechanism: Reject raw prices (non-stationary ranges). Feed a perceptron with MA(1) vs MA(24) geometry in points: inter-MA distances at bars 1/4/7/10; same-MA segment distances 1–4/4–7/7–10; butterfly/envelope (1–10 each MA plus cross 1↔10); quadrilateral; or a complex union. Weights optimized in tester; counter-trend gate requires MA1 above/below MA24 before sell/buy.
data_needed: iMA period 1 and 24, MODE_SMA, PRICE_CLOSE; Point(); optimized weights x/y/z/f in [0,200] step 5
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: H1; five-digit symbols; opt 2010.05.31–2021.05.31 Open prices only; forward 2021.05.31–2022.05.31; TP/SL 60/600 or 200/200 points; lot 0.01
why_new_for_mis: Bounded geometric templates of fast/slow MA configuration—MIS can stream these point-space shape vectors as scale-stable pattern sensors instead of raw OHLC.
quote: I pass all values in points, which is very important since these values have a certain range beyond which they cannot go. Passing a price to a neural network has no sense since it may oscillate in different ranges

mechanism: Instead of screen-dependent angles, compute tg(α)≈Δpoints/Δbars for MA1 and MA24 over spans such as 1–4, 1–5, 1–7, 1–10, and cross-tied slopes between the two MAs. These tangents stay in a bounded range and feed perceptrons (perceptront1–t4) the same way shapes do.
data_needed: MA1/MA24 values at selected bar offsets; division by bar count (not chart pixels)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same H1 MA1/MA24 setup; four-perceptron angle packs tested alongside figure packs
why_new_for_mis: A portable slope/regime-tilt sensor: multi-horizon MA tangents that do not depend on chart zoom—usable as continuous trend-steepness channels for MIS.
quote: rather than calculating the angle, I am going to calculate the angle tangent using the ratio of the number of points to the number of bars

mechanism: Four independent perceptrons (different shapes or different angle sets) must all vote the same sign (all <0 for sell, all >0 for buy) and agree with the MA1↔MA24 counter-trend gate before an order opens—reducing single-template false positives. Forward picks prefer high profit factor with enough trades.
data_needed: Outputs of perceptron1..4 (or t1..t4); MA1[1], MA2[1]; spread filter
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: H1; EA '4 perceptron 4 figure' and '4 perceptron 4 tangent'; complex-criterion and max-profit opts
why_new_for_mis: Treats agreement across heterogeneous geometric sensors as a confidence/regime-consistency bit—MIS can require multi-template consensus before acting on pattern flags.

idea_name: Softmax-thresholded deep net on MA angle/butterfly features
mechanism: DeepNeuralNetwork 4-4-3 or 4-4-4-3 takes four inputs: butterfly envelope distances in points, or four MA1/MA24 slope angles (((v_i-v_j)/Point())/bars). Softmax yields three class shares summing to 100%; trade only if the winning share exceeds LL (e.g. 0.6). Weights/biases sampled randomly in [Min,Max], deduped via CSV across multi-core Passages optimization, then reloaded by pass id for forward trade.
data_needed: MA1/MA24 buffers; 35 (4-4-3) or more weights/biases; OptimizationFileName CSV; LL threshold; Passages index
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; opt 2018.07.12–2021.07.12 Open prices, 10k passes; forward 2021.07.12–2022.07.12 every-tick real ticks; Angle EA beat Figure EA
why_new_for_mis: Upgrades Part-1 geometry into a calibrated 3-way neural sensor (buy/sell/flat) with an explicit confidence floor—MIS can consume softmax mass as tradeability of the current MA-geometry regime.
quote: LL - Softmax function provides 3 results based on 100% sum. 0.6 equals to a value above 60%

idea_name: CSV-deduped random-weight Passages optimizer for NN search
mechanism: Replace exploding multi-input genetic grids with a single Passages counter. OnInit draws random weights/biases (step 0.1), concatenates them to a string, VerifyPassagesInFile skips duplicates, appends new rows under FILE_COMMON, and fills weight[]. Trading mode reloads the row matching Passages. Enables ~1e8 conceptual passes while remembering used parameter vectors.
data_needed: OptimizationFileName in Common\Files; Min/Max; multi-core-safe FileOpen wait loops; tester cache clear between runs
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same EURUSD H1 Angle/Figure/Original EAs; Complex Criterion max
why_new_for_mis: Not a price sensor per se, but a searchable archive of NN weight vectors tied to forward outcomes—MIS can mine which geometry-weight regimes recur as stable across windows.
quote: The main idea is to use only one variable for passes, like a counter of some sort. The remaining parameters of weights and biases are to be set inside the EA.

idea_name: UTC+2 morning session range as multi-symbol breakout sensor
mechanism: For each symbol, RANGER tracks high/low between RangeStart=600 (10:00) and RangeDuration=120 minutes (to 12:00) UTC+2, skipping weekends. After end_time, ask≥range.high or bid≤range.low flags high/low breakout once per day (b_high_breakout / b_low_breakout). SL anchored to opposite side of the range (range volatility).
data_needed: Per-symbol ticks (ask/bid/time); RangeStart/Duration/Close minute offsets; weekend-aware day rolls
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Default Symbols XAUUSD, GBPUSD, USDCAD, USDJPY; tester example on EURUSD 2022.02.01–2022.03.22 every tick; PERIOD_CURRENT stochastic
why_new_for_mis: A clocked intraday liquidity/structure sensor: the morning range envelope and its breach—portable across pairs as a synchronized session-regime channel.
quote: The Expert Advisor begins by calculating the price range between 10:00 AM and 12:00 PM UTC+2, identifying the highest high and lowest low within this timeframe.

idea_name: Stochastic cross confirmation of session-range breakouts
mechanism: CopyBuffer on iStochastic(KPeriod=21). upperBreak = buffer crosses up through upprer_level (80); lowerBreak = crosses down through 100-level (20). BreakOutMode Normal uses upperBreak with high breakout / lowerBreak with low; Reversed_Signal swaps them so high breakout needs oversold cross and low breakout needs overbought cross—filtering false breakouts. Intro frames this as resilience when market regimes shift.
data_needed: Stochastic main line [0],[1]; upprer_level; BreakOutMode enum; range high/low and breakout flags
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi-pair list above; Reversed_Signal + trailing stop enabled in reported test window
why_new_for_mis: Combines a session-structure breach with an oscillator regime cross as a joint change sensor—MIS can require both structure break and momentum-state flip before treating a breakout as regime continuation.
quote: if the price breaks above the previously established high, a potential buy opportunity is triggered. However, for confirmation, the Stochastic Oscillator must be at or below the 20 level

quote: the schedule module does not only allow us to schedule tasks to run after a specific time interval, it also gives us the flexibility to be more specific of when and how a particular task (function) is supposed to run.
